h: How to Fly Like You've Done It Before
p: Nerves are completely normal, and they tend to vanish about three seconds after you lean into the air. The trick is to stay relaxed and let the wind do its job. Bend your knees slightly, keep your head up and your arms in that classic flying shape, and resist the urge to grab at things. The instructor is there to catch you, adjust you and keep you in the middle of the tunnel.

Before you go in, strip off anything loose: jewellery, watches, hair clips and everything in your pockets. Wear trainers with laces and clothes that are comfortable rather than baggy, and tie back long hair. Mention any old injuries, especially shoulders and backs, when you check in. It's also worth eating lightly beforehand, as your stomach will thank you.
Spectators often get just as much out of the visit as the flyers, so bring someone to cheer and film from the viewing area if it's allowed. Photo and video packages are usually offered too.

Birmingham has loads to add on once you've landed. Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery is famous for its Pre-Raphaelite paintings, the Library of Birmingham in Centenary Square is a striking building to look around, and the Jewellery Quarter is a characterful area with independent shops and cafés. Out in Edgbaston, the Birmingham Botanical Gardens make a gentle afternoon, and if you fancy a proper Brummie tea, the city's balti houses are part of its food story. The Black Country Living Museum in nearby Dudley is a superb day out for history fans.
